1.

a machine is a computer that is only yours.

what you get

on usectl a machine is a kubernetes namespace with a resource budget, its own addons, its own domains, its own team and one bill. you never see kubernetes. you see a box with a slider.

  • 1.1

    isolated by default

    its own network policy, its own quota, its own secrets. a neighbour cannot reach you and you cannot reach it.

  • 1.2

    everything inside

    postgres, redis, s3, cron, domains and tls live in the machine, not in five other dashboards.

  • 1.3

    one bill

    a machine's budget is shared by all its apps, addons and groups. adding a second app does not add a second bill.

  • 1.4

    stage and prod

    split a machine into groups, each with its own namespace and its own database, on the same budget.

apps inside a machine can be web, worker or release. each has its own repo, branch, port, replicas and rollout. pr previews get their own namespace and url.

2.

the stack, one toggle each.

specifications · addons

managed on shared platform instances, or dedicated in your own namespace with its own volume and size. attach to any app in one command.

part number addon description
add-pgpostgresmanaged or dedicated. pgvector and timescale on request. scheduled backups to a private bucket.
add-redisredismanaged with a key prefix, or dedicated with aof and search modules.
add-s3s3 storageyour own bucket and iam user on seaweedfs, with a cdn url.
add-natsnatsjetstream on its own volume, websocket in.
add-mongomongodbper machine database, or dedicated.
add-mssqlsql serverfor the apps that need it.
add-meilimeilisearchsearch with its own persistent volume.
add-croncronscheduled jobs from your app image, with run history.
add-oauth2oauth2 proxygithub or google login in front of any app, no code.
add-grafanagrafanadedicated per machine, wired read only to your own telemetry.
add-glitchtipglitchtipsentry compatible error tracking, one dsn per environment.
add-aiaian openai compatible endpoint in the cluster: qwen3-14b for chat, bge-m3 for embeddings, metered per machine.
3.

your agent already knows how to use it.

built for agents

the cli is the product. one binary, every command with --json, clear errors an agent can act on. claude code, cursor, codex or a shell script: they all deploy the same way. there is an mcp server if you prefer tool calls.

  • 3.1

    deploy from the chat

    usectl machines create, usectl deploy, usectl logs --follow. no plugin needed.

  • 3.2

    agents that live here

    add a hermes or openclaw pod to a machine and it runs 24/7 with its own memory, its own headless browser and a local model. one agent, one machine, its own walls.

  • 3.3

    read what happened

    logs, metrics, traces and pod insights through the same cli, so the agent that deployed can also debug.

4.

on our metal, or on yours.

one product, two rooms
  • 4.1 · mode a

    managed

    we run it. bare metal we own in falkenstein, kubernetes we operate, backups, ingress, tls and the 3am pager on us. you push git.

  • 4.2 · mode b

    self hosted

    you run it. the same platform on your own hardware, your data never leaves the building. self hosted usectl ships this month.

same cli, same addons, same one command. the only choice is whose room the box stands in.

people who run many things.

who it is for

7.

push git. get https.

how it ships · deploy sequence
  1. connect a repo through the github app, or push from the cli.
  2. we detect next.js, vite, node or static and build it in the cluster with kaniko. or bring your own dockerfile.
  3. the app goes live at https://name.usectl.com with a certificate. add your own domain in one command.
  4. every deploy keeps history. roll back without a rebuild. auto rollback watches for 5xx after a deploy.
8.

customer zero

reference design · in production

systemctl runs its own 9 person software shop on usectl: 133 deployments, an ev charging platform with 16 services, a taxi app, a clinic, online shops, and the agents that run our socials.

we built usectl because we needed it. every client we ship gets its own machine, and when it breaks at night it is our pager, not theirs.

9.

questions people ask

application notes
  • an-1

    is a machine a vm?

    no. it is a kubernetes namespace with a network policy, a quota and its own secrets on nodes we operate. container isolation, not a microvm. we say that plainly because it matters for some workloads.

  • an-2

    can i leave?

    yes. your dockerfile, your postgres dump and your bucket run anywhere. if we disappeared tomorrow your stack still works.

  • an-3

    where is my data?

    on bare metal we own at hetzner in falkenstein, germany. with self hosted usectl, on your own hardware.

  • an-4

    what about backups?

    managed postgres is dumped nightly at the platform level. dedicated postgres gets scheduled backups to a private bucket only that database can reach.

  • an-5

    is there a bandwidth meter or a seat fee?

    no and no. the sticker is the ceiling.

  • an-6

    do i need docker?

    not for next.js, vite, node or static sites. for anything else, a dockerfile.
